headline: Record highs on a soft jobs report, but rate-path odds stay contested
body: Equities extended a strong run this week, with the S&P 500 closing at a fresh record above 7,750 and the Nasdaq up more than 5% for the week, as traders leaned into a surprise 23,000-job contraction in July payrolls -- a miss wide enough (Wall Street had penciled in roughly +83,000) that it reads as reassurance the Fed won't need to tighten further, more than fresh alarm about the labor market. Leadership stayed concentrated in AI-adjacent names -- Nvidia and Salesforce were among the session's better performers -- while more rate- and commodity-sensitive names like Chevron and Caterpillar lagged, a pattern consistent with a market still rewarding growth over cyclicals.

Retail chatter is leaning the same direction as the tape rather than against it: AI and momentum names (Nvidia, Nebius, AST SpaceMobile) dominate today's most-discussed tickers, with no clear rotation into hedges or defensive names showing up in the noise. The bigger swing factor for the week ahead looks less like price action and more like the rate path itself -- coverage is notably split on how hawkish or dovish the Fed actually is heading into its September meeting, with upcoming CPI and employment data cited repeatedly as the real tie-breaker. That's a setup where the rally has been resilient on positioning, but hasn't really been tested by a hawkish inflation surprise yet.
